newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian barley pool prices cut by A$10/t.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian barley pool prices cut by A$10/t.

text.p: The Australian Barley Board has reduced its estimates of pool returns for malting and feed barley by A$10.00 a tonne because of big crops around the world, general manager Michael Iwaniw said in a statement.
Forecast malting barley returns have been reduced to A$220 a tonne while feed barley forecast returns are down to A$167 a tonne in Victoria.
"(The price cuts) present the reality of very large increases in world grain supply without a matching increase in demand," Iwaniw said.

Production of barley this year had been enormous, with the European crop now 90 percent harvested and about six million tonnes more than last year, yielding particularly well in malting barley areas, he said.
Six million tonnes was more than the entire Australian barley crop, he said.

Australia's major export competitor Canada was now harvesting a 16 million tonne barley crop. This had major implications for the export malting market and the international feed grain trade, he said.

The quality of the European barley crop was well ahead of expectations and would secure the European market and leave a surplus for export, placing considerable downward pressure on prices, Iwaniw said.

Corn from the U.S. was the major competing feed grain and firming crop estimates in the U.S. had seen corn futures drifting steadily downward, with feed barley prices from Canada and elsewhere responding accordingly, he said.
Small amounts of subsidies were creeping into European sales and this raised great concern about future subsidy activity, both in the malt pipeline and for direct sales of feed barley, he said.
Key factors determining how barley prices move over coming months would be the finaol size of the U.S. corn crop, European policy on export subsidies and Canadian selling strategies, he said.
Positive crop forecasts in Australia confirm the view that export market developments will drive all Australian prices, he said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
